```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(newhallrs)
```

This vignette shows the main ways to run the Newhall simulation: from a
data frame, from CSV files, in strict mode, with the hydrothermal model, and
on a `terra::SpatRaster`.

## Input data

Each row is a site with latitude (`latDD`), longitude (`lonDD`), available
water capacity (`awc`), elevation (`elev`), monthly mean temperature
(`tJan` to `tDec`, deg C) and monthly precipitation (`pJan` to `pDec`, mm).

```{r data}
temps <- rbind(
  c(-2.9, -1.7, 3.2, 9.4, 15.1, 19.9, 22.1, 21.3, 17.2, 10.9, 5.2, -0.3),
  c(22.1, 22.0, 20.9, 18.2, 15.2, 12.8, 12.0, 13.1, 15.3, 17.6, 19.4, 21.1),
  c(-3.5, -3.5, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 7.5, 7.5, 7.5, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, -3.5),
  c(9, 11, 15, 19, 24, 29, 31, 30, 26, 20, 14, 10)
)
precips <- rbind(
  rep(85, 12),
  c(102, 118, 130, 127, 120, 132, 97, 81, 69, 77, 84, 78),
  rep(75, 12),
  rep(8, 12)
)
colnames(temps) <- paste0("t", month.abb)
colnames(precips) <- paste0("p", month.abb)

df <- cbind(
  data.frame(
    latDD = c(40.8, -33.8688, 48.0, 33.4),
    lonDD = c(-77.8, 151.2093, -110.0, -112.0),
    awc = c(200, 200, 200, 150),
    elev = c(350, 19, 1200, 330)
  ),
  as.data.frame(temps),
  as.data.frame(precips)
)
```

## 1. Tabular workflow

`newhall_batch()` on a data frame returns one row of results per site.

```{r tabular}
res <- newhall_batch(df)
res[, c("temperatureRegime", "moistureRegime")]
```

## 2. CSV workflow

Pass one or more CSV paths. Files are read and row-bound, then run as above.
Here we use temporary files.

```{r csv}
csv1 <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
csv2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(df[1:2, ], csv1, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(df[3:4, ], csv2, row.names = FALSE)

res_csv <- newhall_batch(c(csv1, csv2))
all.equal(res_csv, res)
```

`newhall_batch_hydrothermal()` accepts paths too. Hydrothermal CSVs can also
carry monthly snow depth columns (`snowJan` to `snowDec`, m).

```{r csv-hydrothermal}
df4 <- df
for (m in month.abb) df4[[paste0("snow", m)]] <- 0
df4$snowJan[3] <- 0.8

csv4 <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
utils::write.csv(df4, csv4, row.names = FALSE)
res4_csv <- newhall_batch_hydrothermal(csv4)
res4_csv[, c("temperatureRegime", "moistureRegime")]
unlink(c(csv1, csv2, csv4))
```

## 3. Strict mode

`strict = TRUE` uses the defect-remediated `StrictNewhall` physics instead of
the classic jNSM-compatible `ClassicNewhall` model. Compare it with the
default run on the regime columns.

```{r strict}
res_strict <- newhall_batch(df, strict = TRUE)
regime_cols <- c("temperatureRegime", "moistureRegime")
cmp <- data.frame(
  default_temp = res$temperatureRegime,
  strict_temp = res_strict$temperatureRegime,
  default_moist = res$moistureRegime,
  strict_moist = res_strict$moistureRegime
)
cmp
identical(res[regime_cols], res_strict[regime_cols])
```

The last line shows whether strict mode changed any regime for these sites.

## 4. Hydrothermal workflow

`newhall_batch_hydrothermal()` adds 1D soil thermal and water-table physics.
Site level parameters such as `zWt` (water-table depth, m) and
`oHorizonThickness` (m) can be columns in the data frame.

```{r hydrothermal}
df4$zWt <- c(0.3, 100, 100, 100)
df4$oHorizonThickness <- c(0, 0, 0.12, 0)

res4 <- newhall_batch_hydrothermal(df4)
setdiff(names(res4), names(res))
res4[, c("temperatureRegime", "moistureRegime")]
```

## 5. Raster workflow

With the `terra` package installed, a `SpatRaster` whose layers are named like
the data frame columns can be run directly. The result is a raster with one
layer per output column. These chunks are skipped when `terra` is not
available.

```{r raster-input, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
nr <- 5L
nc <- 2L
idx <- rep(seq_len(nrow(df)), length.out = nr * nc)
grid <- df[idx, ]
layers <- lapply(names(grid), function(nm) {
  terra::rast(
    nrows = nr, ncols = nc,
    xmin = -100, xmax = -98, ymin = 38, ymax = 40,
    crs = "EPSG:4326", vals = grid[[nm]]
  )
})
r <- terra::rast(layers)
names(r) <- names(grid)
r
```

```{r raster-classic, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
out <- newhall_batch(r, nrows = 2L)
terra::nlyr(out)
names(out)
```

```{r raster-hydrothermal, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
out4 <- newhall_batch_hydrothermal(r, nrows = 2L)
terra::nlyr(out4)
setdiff(names(out4), names(out))
```
